title: Structs, struct tags and JSON serialisation

videos.script: Lesson 14 found values by a key that could be any string. A struct is the other way to group values. The names are fixed, and the compiler knows every one of them. {{struct}} You will declare a struct, fill one in with a literal, and compare two of them. Then the cases where comparing is refused. {{marshal}} After that, a struct goes out as JSON. The field names become the keys. A field that starts with a lower-case letter disappears from the output, and nothing tells you. {{tags}} A tag is a short string after a field. It renames the key, drops the field when it is empty, or keeps it out of the JSON for good. A tag with a typo is ignored too, so go vet gets a turn. {{unmarshal}} Last, JSON coming in. Unknown keys are skipped, missing ones stay at zero, and the names match in either case. By the end you can say exactly what crosses the boundary, in both directions, and what stays behind.
